newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: NATO denies deal with Russia on Slovak membership.
newsitem.headline: NATO denies deal with Russia on Slovak membership.

text.p: A senior NATO official on Thursday denied a claim by Slovak Premier Vladimir Meciar that the U.S. and Russia had reached an agreement omitting Slovakia from the first wave of the security alliance's expansion.

Anthony Cragg, deputy secretary general of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, said during a meeting with Slovak President Michal Kovac that reports of a deal between the two superpowers on NATO enlargement was only speculation, presidential spokesman Vladimir Stefko said.
"(Cragg) said that the U.S. and the Russian Federation could not, and did not conclude any agreement omitting Slovakia from the process of (NATO) acceptance," Stefko told Reuters.
Slovakia, roundly criticised by the European Union and NATO countries for slow progress on the path to democracy, has lately been left out of official statements on first-wave expansion candidates.
Meciar recently told a party rally in Trnava, western Slovakia, that Slovakia's exclusion from NATO was part of a "global pact" between the U.S. and Russia.
"Mr Cragg said the question of new NATO members will be solved by an agreement between all 16 allies...even the most powerful members can't make such a decision alon e," Stefko said.
The Meciar government has repeatedly proclaimed its ambition to be among the first wave of potential NATO members, but some statements since have indicated some doubts within the coalition.
Last week President Kovac called a referendum for May on NATO membership at the instigation of the opposition.
The referendum pits Kovac against Meciar, avowed political foes. Kovac has accused Meciar of deceiving and misleading the public on the issue, questioning his democratic credentials.
